name: David Hasselhoff
milestone_by_age_26: Landed a regular leading role as Dr. Snapper Foster on the CBS soap opera The Young and the Restless in December 1975, which he held for six years.
early_history_summary: Hasselhoff made his theatrical debut at age seven in Peter Pan and pursued acting throughout school, serving as president of the choir and holding lead roles in plays. He studied theater at the California Institute of the Arts until 1973, then landed his first major television role on The Young and the Restless in late 1975 at age 23, replacing William Gray Espy as Snapper Foster.
family_context_summary: Son of a business executive father and homemaker mother; middle-class Roman Catholic family that moved frequently during his childhood.
evidence_summary: Hasselhoff trained at the California Institute of the Arts and leveraged the 1970s network soap opera boom to land a regular role on a CBS daytime show at age 23. His father was a business executive, providing a middle-class upbringing, but no family entertainment-industry connections are documented. His early theater experience from age seven and formal training at CalArts gave him the acting chops to audition successfully for network television.

name: Roman Abramovich
milestone_by_age_26: No material business milestone by age 26 found. Abramovich was trading plastic ducks, perfumes, and small commodities under perestroika and was arrested in June 1992 (age 25) for diesel fuel theft, but his material wealth breakthrough came at age 29 with the Sibneft acquisition in 1995.
early_history_summary: Orphaned by age 4 and raised by relatives in northern Russia, Abramovich left school at 16, served in the Soviet Army, and began small-scale trading under perestroika in the late 1980s. By the early 1990s he had started and liquidated at least 20 small companies in various sectors, but his oligarch-level wealth only materialized after partnering with Boris Berezovsky in 1993-1994.
family_context_summary: Orphaned at age 4; mother died of sepsis when he was 1, father killed in a construction accident when he was 3. Raised by maternal aunt and uncle in Ukhta, Komi Republic, sharing a three-room flat.
evidence_summary: Abramovich's early business activities by age 26 were small-scale commodity trading and company formation under perestroika, not a material milestone. His defining wealth event was the 1995 Sibneft acquisition at age 29, facilitated by Boris Berezovsky's political connections. He was orphaned at age 4 and raised by relatives in northern Russia with limited means.

name: Michael Houghton
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Houghton was completing his PhD studies at King's College London (PhD awarded 1977, age 28); his co-discovery of hepatitis C came in 1989 at age 40.
early_history_summary: Houghton studied at the University of East Anglia (BSc) and then pursued a PhD at King's College London, completing his thesis on RNA polymerases in 1977. His landmark co-discovery of hepatitis C occurred much later in 1989 at Chiron Corporation.
evidence_summary: Houghton was a graduate student through his mid-twenties, with no material scientific milestone by age 26. His Nobel Prize-winning discovery of hepatitis C came at age 40 in 1989. No family background or early advantage information was found in reviewed sources.

name: Horst Ludwig Störmer
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Störmer was a graduate student at the time; his PhD was awarded in 1977 (age 28), and his Nobel Prize-winning fractional quantum Hall effect experiments came in the 1980s.
early_history_summary: Störmer studied physics at Goethe University Frankfurt after initially enrolling in architectural engineering, then moved to Grenoble for his PhD research in a high-magnetic field laboratory. His PhD was awarded by the University of Stuttgart in 1977, after which he joined Bell Labs where his Nobel-winning work was conducted.
evidence_summary: Störmer was a physics graduate student through his mid-twenties with no material milestone by age 26. His Nobel Prize-winning work on the fractional quantum Hall effect was conducted at Bell Labs in the 1980s, well after age 26. name: Rivaldo
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for FC Barcelona in 1997 at age 25 as a 17 million pound replacement for Ronaldo, going on to win consecutive La Liga titles in 1998 and 1999.
early_history_summary: Growing up in a favela in Recife, Rivaldo joined Santa Cruz's youth setup at age 11 and made his senior debut in 1991 at age 19. He progressed through Mogi Mirim, Corinthians (loan), and Palmeiras, winning the Brazilian national championship in 1994, before moving to Deportivo La Coruna in 1996 and then Barcelona in 1997 at age 25.
family_context_summary: Born into a working-class family in a favela on the outskirts of Recife, Brazil. His father Romildo gave him his first football boots at age 13 and encouraged his football career; his mother Marlucia also urged him to pursue football professionally after his father's passing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father gave him his first boots and encouraged football; family had no professional football connections but was immersed in the local football culture of Recife.
evidence_summary: Rivaldo rose from extreme poverty in a Recife favela to sign for FC Barcelona at age 25, overcoming bow-leggedness and a 30km daily walk to training at Santa Cruz. His father gave him his first boots at 13 and encouraged the football path before passing away. The Brazilian football pipeline from Santa Cruz to Palmeiras to Deportivo to Barcelona provided the institutional ladder, but his physical talent and relentless dedication were the primary drivers. He won the Brazilian championship with Palmeiras in 1994 and Olympic bronze in 1996 before the Barcelona signing.

name: Uli Hoeneß
milestone_by_age_26: Won three consecutive Bundesliga titles (1972-1974), three consecutive European Cups (1974-1976), the 1972 European Championship, and the 1974 FIFA World Cup with West Germany, all by age 24; scored twice in the 1974 European Cup final replay.
early_history_summary: Hoeneß played youth football at VfB Ulm from age 7 and TSG Ulm 1846 from age 13. He was recruited by Bayern Munich manager Udo Lattek in 1970 at age 18, immediately earning a regular spot alongside Beckenbauer, Maier, and Müller. He won his first DFB Cup in 1971 and his first Bundesliga title in 1972 at age 20.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Born in Ulm, West Germany; brother was also involved in football.
evidence_summary: Hoeneß joined Bayern Munich at 18 and immediately integrated into a legendary squad featuring Beckenbauer, Müller, and Maier under coach Udo Lattek. By age 20 he won his first Bundesliga title, and by 24 he had three European Cups, a World Cup, and a European Championship. His youth career from age 7 at VfB Ulm and TSG Ulm 1846 provided the foundation for recruitment to Bayern. No family financial or domain background is documented in reviewed sources.

name: Martin Scorsese
milestone_by_age_26: His feature film directorial debut, Who's That Knocking at My Door, premiered at the Chicago International Film Festival in November 1967 at age 25, earning a glowing review from Roger Ebert.
early_history_summary: Scorsese grew up in Little Italy, Manhattan, with asthma that prevented sports, leading his parents to take him to movie theaters where he developed a passion for cinema. He made short films at NYU under professor Haig Manoogian, earned his BA in 1964 and MA in 1968, and shot his first feature over 1965-1967 with fellow students Harvey Keitel and Thelma Schoonmaker.
family_context_summary: Both parents worked in the Garment District — father was a clothes presser and actor, mother was a seamstress and actress. Working-class Italian-American family in Little Italy, Manhattan. All four grandparents were Italian immigrants from Sicily.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not film professionals but both acted amateurishly; father took Scorsese to see films including Jean Renoir's The River, which fascinated him. No direct industry connections transferred.
evidence_summary: Scorsese's asthmatic childhood in Little Italy channeled him into cinema obsession, and NYU film school under Haig Manoogian provided the mentorship and seed money ($5,000) for his first feature. The film premiered at the Chicago International Film Festival in 1967 when he was 25, earning Roger Ebert's first published review calling it 'a great moment in American movies.' His working-class Italian-American family had no film industry connections, but growing up in Little Italy gave him deep domain material. He connected with the 'movie brats' circle (De Palma, Coppola, Lucas, Spielberg) during this period.

name: Brian May
milestone_by_age_26: Queen's self-titled debut album was released on 13 July 1973 by EMI Records when May was 25, featuring four songs he wrote including the single 'Keep Yourself Alive.'
early_history_summary: May won a scholarship to Hampton Grammar School at 11, formed his first band '1984' with Tim Staffell as a teenager, and built his signature Red Special guitar with his father. He graduated from Imperial College London with a BSc in physics in 1968, formed Smile with Roger Taylor that year, and co-founded Queen with Freddie Mercury in 1970. The debut album was recorded 1971-1972 and released in July 1973.
family_context_summary: Only child of Harold May, a draughtsman at the Ministry of Aviation, and Ruth Irving (née Fletcher), who was Scottish. Middle-class family in Hampton Hill, Middlesex. Father helped build the Red Special guitar that became May's signature instrument.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a draughtsman whose engineering skills directly enabled the construction of the Red Special guitar, May's signature instrument throughout his career. No music industry connections in the family.
evidence_summary: May's middle-class upbringing and his father's draughtsmanship skills enabled the construction of the Red Special guitar, his signature instrument. He won a scholarship to a grammar school, studied physics at Imperial College, and leveraged London's position as the center of rock music in the late 1960s. The formation of Queen with Freddie Mercury and Roger Taylor in 1970 created one of rock's greatest collaborative teams. The debut album release in July 1973 at age 25 was the material milestone, riding the 1970s rock wave.

name: Javier Solana
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Solana was a Fulbright Scholar studying physics at US universities (PhD awarded 1971, age 29); his political career took off in 1976 when he was elected to PSOE's Federal Executive Commission at age 34.
early_history_summary: Solana studied at Complutense University, clandestinely joined the PSOE in 1964, and went to the US on a Fulbright Scholarship in 1965, studying at the University of Chicago, UC San Diego, and the University of Virginia. He received his physics doctorate from Virginia in 1971 and returned to Spain as a lecturer.
family_context_summary: Comes from a prominent Spanish family; father was a chemistry professor who died when Javier was 19. First cousin twice removed of diplomat Salvador de Madariaga. Elder brother Luis was imprisoned for political activities opposing Franco and later became a telecommunications industry leader.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a chemistry professor (academic domain), and the family had prominent diplomatic and intellectual connections through the de Madariaga family. Brother was a political activist and Trilateral Commission member.
evidence_summary: Solana was a graduate student in physics through his mid-twenties with no material milestone by age 26. His PhD was awarded in 1971 at age 29, and his significant political career began in 1976 at age 34. He came from a prominent Spanish family with academic and diplomatic connections, but these did not produce a material milestone by 26.

name: Grigory Margulis
milestone_by_age_26: Received the Moscow Mathematical Society young mathematicians prize in 1968 at age 22 and co-proved the Kazhdan-Margulis theorem, a foundational result on discrete groups published the same year.
early_history_summary: Margulis won a silver medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad at age 16 in 1962 and enrolled at Moscow State University the same year. He began research in ergodic theory under Yakov Sinai, co-proved the Kazhdan-Margulis theorem with David Kazhdan, and received the Moscow Mathematical Society's young mathematicians prize in 1968, all before completing his PhD in 1970 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Born to a Russian family of Lithuanian Jewish descent in Moscow, Soviet Union. No family financial or academic background documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Margulis showed exceptional mathematical ability early, winning an IMO silver medal at 16 and enrolling at Moscow State University, one of the world's elite math institutions. Under Yakov Sinai's supervision, he co-proved the Kazhdan-Margulis theorem and won the Moscow Mathematical Society's young mathematicians prize by age 22. He later faced antisemitism in the Soviet system, being unable to secure a position at Moscow University despite being a top young mathematician. His PhD in 1970 at age 24 further confirmed his trajectory toward the 1978 Fields Medal.

name: Carlos Sainz
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Spanish Rally Championship in 1987 at age 25 with a Ford Sierra RS Cosworth, and made his World Rally Championship debut the same year with Ford.
early_history_summary: Sainz began rallying in 1980 at age 18, won the inaugural Copa Panda one-make rally series in 1981, became SEAT's official pilot in 1982, and progressed through the Spanish Rally Championship. He finished runner-up in 1986 and won the championship in 1987 and 1988, earning his first WRC appearances with Ford in 1987.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Born in Madrid; sister Carmen provided his first driving experience in a SEAT 600 at age 11. Was a Spanish squash champion at 16 and received a Real Madrid football trial as a teenager.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Sister's SEAT 600 provided early driving exposure but no family motorsport connections are documented.
evidence_summary: Sainz entered rallying at 18 and rapidly progressed through Spain's national rally scene, winning the Copa Panda in 1981 and the Spanish Rally Championship by 1987 at age 25. His athletic versatility (Spanish squash champion at 16, Real Madrid football trial) suggests natural physical talent. The SEAT official pilot program provided early equipment access and a competitive pipeline. No family financial or motorsport background is documented. His WRC debut in 1987 with Ford set the stage for his two world championships in 1990 and 1992.

name: Alain Aspect
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Aspect passed the agregation in physics in 1969 and received his PhD in 1971 (age 24), then taught in Cameroon for three years; his Nobel Prize-winning Bell test experiments were conducted 1980-1982 at age 33-35.
early_history_summary: Aspect graduated from the Ecole Normale Superieure de Cachan, passed the agregation in physics in 1969, and received his PhD from the Ecole superieure d'optique of Universite d'Orsay in 1971. He then taught in Cameroon for three years as a replacement for military service before returning to France to begin his habilitation research on Bell test experiments in the early 1980s.
evidence_summary: Aspect was a graduate student and then a teacher in Cameroon through his mid-twenties, with no material scientific milestone by age 26.
